system.summary: Each number 1-682 is the position of a character in 13 printed lines of Dumas's 1775 preface to Vattel, Le Droit des gens; every occurrence of a letter is an alternative number for it.

diacritics.note: Accents ignored in use; apostrophes, hyphens, commas, full stops, & and the reference mark are counted as characters and used.

prior_solution.where: The key and system: Dumas's letter of 30 April 1776 (Franklin Papers 22:403-412) and S. Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, 'Dumas' Cipher - Benjamin Franklin's Favorite Cipher' (2008-09), who re-established Dumas's own key text of 1776 from the Committee's enciphering table. Decoded passages in print: Franklin Papers 22, Sparks 9, Force 5th ser. 2, Wharton 2-4. Contemporary decipherments interlined on most pages (unpublished for the passages the editions leave out).

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents. The recount, the key replay, the re-marking of the readings and the reading reviews of 24 Nov 2026 were made by an AI agent for the maintainers; no person has checked a reading.
tools: Python transcription-reconciliation, decoding and test scripts (scripts/, key/, tests/)
image crops of the NARA Catalog images

solution.what: Fetched PCC item 93 vol. 1 (503 images) and the M332 roll 2 Dumas file (211 images) from the NARA Catalog at a person's pace; item 93 vols. 2-4 screened on contact sheets only.
Found the key system in Dumas's 30 April 1776 letter (line totals, counting rule) and Tomokiyo's transcription of the 13 key lines on Cryptiana.
Built the 682-position key from the 1830 reprint of the preface adjusted to Dumas's line totals and Tomokiyo's wording; froze it (sha256 36276e0a...).

Test 1: key built from the 1778 glosses on M332 images 9, 10, 13 predicted the glosses on image 20: 106 of 108 (200 shuffled keys: mean 7.9%, max 14.8%). Test 2 (plan written first): the printed-text key against the glosses on item 93 image 173: 129 of 134 (129 of 130 sure glosses); 200 shuffled keys mean 7.1%, max 14.9%.
Every cipher run transcribed twice by independent passes (forward and backward), about 6,900 number places; about 95% agreed before image checks; the rest settled on crops.
Decoded and read all 21 items; emendations marked; print checked passage by passage in the Franklin Papers (partly), Sparks 9 and Wharton 2-3.

A second AI agent of ours rebuilt the key from Cryptiana (one difference in 682, position 515, a typing slip on the page), transcribed four passages on its own with the same numbers and readings, and redid the print check in Wharton 2-4, Sparks 9 and Force. Corrections applied: 1776 despatch D images 52-53 are in Force; 641 is the V. of 'Madam V. Loder'; 2 Aug 1777 L12 is 14, not 12; wording of May 1779 and 20 Sept 1779.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 4129 tokens, 678 types, fr-1750-nospace order 4: reading -2.008 per letter; random keys -5.269 (z 39.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.454 (mean -3.482, z 85.9); annealer on the real text -3.528. Verdict: pass.

Maintainer's check before merging pull request #667 (review of 15 Nov 2026): a position table built from key/keytext_1775.txt was identical to key_positions.json; a separate decoder on all 29 reconciled files gave the folder's letters except at the marked emendations; test 2 re-ran at 129 of 134; on the National Archives Catalog images the numbers of three passages the editions omit (2 Aug 1777, 25 Sept 1777, 2 Sept 1781: 108 numbers) agreed number for number.

Key replay (docs/_replay.py, replay.py): key/key_positions.json applied to the 4,503 number places of the principal copies and compared with the cipher passages of letters/*_text.txt: 4,479 give the reading's letter exactly and one more is c written for k; 18 are marked emendations; 1 is unread (the guessed & of 20 Sept 1779); 4 have no key value (three blots; 698, out of range). No unmarked difference. The first run found five: three places where the cipher repeats the plain word before it (2 Aug 1777 le, 14 Aug 1777 à, 24 Feb 1778 des), Pensionnaire for the numbers' Pensionaire, and mérit(ent); the readings were corrected.

Read share recounted by the README rules of 16-19 Nov 2026 (cipher words only, holes by words, a corrected or supplied letter is a hole). The reading files were re-marked: cipher between the cipher marks, [x] for a hole, {+x} for a letter given by another cipher copy or by the decipherer's letter over the number. 928 of 948 cipher words, 20 holes; every entry at 0.95 or more except 12 Apr 1777 (18 of 19) and 20 Sept 1779 (4 of 6), which are read by the short-text floor. The extract of despatch C (1776) is at 31 of 32 with the decipherer's letters counted and at 27 of 32 by the key alone.

Six pages looked at again on the National Archives Catalog images (item 93 vol. 1 images 41, 55, 81, 108, 160, 493): the numbers of the bare sentences of 25 Sept 1777 (32) and 2 Sept 1781 (13) and of run 2 of 2 Aug 1777 (43) are as transcribed; on image 41 the decipherer's u stands over 84, his e over the blotted second number of line 17 and a short stroke over 163, and the number of the g of chargé is under a blot; on image 160 the last number of line 24 is a clear 54; on image 55 the blotted number shows a first figure 5, and the letter over it (b or l) has its foot in the blot. The folder's image numbers follow the catalog's object ids; the catalog's own object list has two objects out of place (objects 73 and 170 of the list), so that images 73 to 216 are one place later in it.

Prior art looked at again. Cryptiana's page gives the key text and decodes none of the letters. The Internet Archive texts of Sparks vol. 9 and Wharton vols. 2-3 searched by date and by keyword for the ten passage groups: Sparks prints 14 Oct 1777, 15 May 1779 and the postscript of 2 Sept 1781 without their cipher sentences, and has no letter of 2 Aug, 25 Sept, 4 Nov or 28 Nov 1777, 24 Feb, 27 Apr or 14 June 1778, or 21 June 1779; no letter of those dates and none of the passages' wording in Wharton 2-3. Web searches for the passages (Founders Online included) found nothing. OCR texts, searched, not read page by page. Not checked: the Adams Papers volumes and any letterbook copy kept by Dumas.

Reading review by the maintainers' integration reviewer (an AI agent, not a person): the 18 readings read as sentences against their translations, with the replay and the six images above; grades recorded in outcome.texts in place of the author's preliminary ones (16 A, 2 B: the extract of despatch C of 1776 and 20 Sept 1779).

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.008; polyphony 0.0; 1 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.528

outcome.method_basis: Key text and system from Dumas's 1776 letter and Tomokiyo's transcription, tested against the contemporary glosses; every cipher run in the Dumas letters of PCC item 93 vol. 1 and M332 roll 2 transcribed twice and decoded.

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: inventory of every cipher passage in the Dumas letters of PCC item 93 vol. 1 and M332 roll 2, double transcriptions, the test of the printed key against the contemporary glosses, and the text of the passages the editions leave out. Reading with a known key, not a break.

The Committee's decipherer or decipherers, who wrote letters over the numbers on most pages (faint pencil in 1776, ink later). Hand not identified; the letter forms are compatible with James Lovell's, which is not an identification. Their glosses were used to test the key and to settle doubtful numbers.

Member of the Committee of Secret Correspondence to which the 1776 despatches were addressed; Dumas set out the key and the counting rule for it in his letter of 30 April 1776; Franklin used the cipher himself (to Dumas, 16 Aug 1781).

Satoshi Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, 'Dumas' Cipher - Benjamin Franklin's Favorite Cipher' (2008-09): re-established Dumas's own 13-line key text of 1776 from the Committee's enciphering table, the line totals and the homophonic system. Our key agrees with his page in 681 of 682 positions (515, a typing slip on the page).

Papers of Benjamin Franklin vol. 22: the 30 April and 14 May 1776 letters with the cipher passages decoded in brackets, from the interlined decoding. Two readings corrected here: "France" for "fiance" (571 = r, glossed r); "Les alliés" for "Des alliés" (70 = l by the key; the contemporary gloss looks like d, so the slip was the decipherer's and the editors followed it).
Diplomatic Correspondence of the American Revolution vol. 9: translations including the decoded content of the printed letters; leaves out the passages listed in NOTES.
American Archives, 5th ser., vol. 2, cols. 99-103: despatch D of Sept-Oct 1776 with the numbers, an interlined decipherment and a translation (images 52-53, "le ministre même", "Madam V. Loder").
Revolutionary Diplomatic Correspondence vols. 2-4: translations of the printed letters, the cipher content included where Sparks had it; lists the omitted letters of 1777.

texts.label: 30 April 1776 and the copied unsigned letter of 6/9 May (in print)
texts.summary: Dumas reports opening himself to a French minister at The Hague, the request for French mediation or a Bourbon alliance, and the minister's fear that reconciled colonies would turn on their helpers. Printed decoded in the Franklin Papers 22:403-412.
texts.note: Read share over the cipher words only (the words between the cipher marks of the reading file; research/reading_audit measure, 24 Nov 2026): a word with a letter corrected or supplied by sense is a hole. 305 cipher words, 2 holes: e[t] and d[e], letters written in neither copy. Three words take a letter from the Extrait copy (Angleterr{+e}: the letter has 698, out of range, the copy 658; q{+u}'on; réconcilie{+n}t). By numbers: 1,463 of 1,464 give the reading's letter as transcribed.

reading_review.by: integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading; it replaces the preliminary B recorded by the author's agents on 14 Nov 2026. The reading file read as sentences, with the clear words around the cipher runs, against the English translation: coherent French throughout (the rentiers in the English funds and the courts that side with England; France and Spain as the allies that suit; the opening to a French minister, his fear that reconciled colonies would turn on their helpers, "les chiens de la fable"; the two questions on mediation and a Bourbon alliance; the unsigned note about the fair at The Hague). Two holes in 305 cipher words, each a single letter of a two-letter word. Not checked by the reviewer: the images of this letter, and the Franklin Papers text beyond what NOTES reports. The key replay (replay.py, replay.tsv) decodes every number of the principal copy with key/key_positions.json: each letter of the reading that the key does not give is marked. A model's reading: no person has checked it.

texts.label: Despatch B, 14 May-6 June 1776 (in print)
texts.summary: The French minister's answer of 21 May 1776: no mediation while the colonies are the King of England's subjects and no alliance while France is at peace, but Americans may buy arms and munitions in France as merchandise; Hortalez will apply to the Committee. Printed decoded in the Franklin Papers 22:433-436.
texts.note: Read share over the cipher words only (the words between the cipher marks of the reading file; research/reading_audit measure, 24 Nov 2026): a word with a letter corrected or supplied by sense is a hole. 223 cipher words, 6 holes, each one letter: l[i]eu, parol[e], de[s], gu[e]rre, m[o]urir, Fran[c]e (the numbers are clear to both passes and give another letter, or the letter is not written; no letter of the decipherer was read over them). By numbers: 996 of 1,001 give the reading's letter as transcribed.

reading_review.by: integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading; it replaces the preliminary B recorded by the author's agents on 14 Nov 2026. The reading file read as sentences against the English translation: coherent French throughout (the offer of expenses; the minister's answer of 21 May: no mediation while the colonies are subjects of the King of England, no alliance while France is at peace, but Americans may buy arms and munitions in France as merchandise; "One Hortalez" will apply). Six holes in 223 cipher words, all single letters in words whose sense is not in doubt and which the Franklin Papers print corrected. Not checked by the reviewer: the images of this letter. The key replay (replay.py, replay.tsv) decodes every number of the principal copy with key/key_positions.json: each letter of the reading that the key does not give is marked. A model's reading: no person has checked it.

texts.label: Despatch C, extract, summer 1776 (in print)
texts.summary: The name Hortalez (spelled "Hortelez" in the numbers) and Dumas's plan to present himself also at the Spanish embassy; printed in Sparks 9 and Wharton 2.
texts.note: Read share over the cipher words only (the words between the cipher marks of the reading file; research/reading_audit measure, 24 Nov 2026): a word with a letter corrected or supplied by sense is a hole. 32 cipher words, 1 hole: char[g]é (the number is under a blot). Four more words take one letter from the contemporary decipherer's letters written over the numbers, which count as plain text beside the cipher: Hort{+a}lez (29 = e), d'Espagne (163 = b where the apostrophe is wanted), simpl{+e}ment (40 = y, second figure blotted), p{+u}issance (84 = d). By the key alone the extract stands at 27 of 32 (0.844), under the bar: its class rests on the decipherer's letters. By numbers: 162 of 168 give the reading's letter as transcribed; one is a blot.

reading_review.by: integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading; it replaces the preliminary B recorded by the author's agents on 14 Nov 2026. The reading file read as sentences against the English translation: coherent (Lee on the French gentleman "Hortalez"; Dumas means to present himself at the Spanish embassy too, so as not to neglect "une puissance si digne aussi de leur confiance"). B, not A: in 32 cipher words one is a hole and four lean on the decipherer's letters, so the extract is the weakest of the set. The reviewer looked at image 41 (National Archives Catalog, 24 Nov 2026): the decipherer's u stands over 84, his e over the blotted second number of line 17, a short stroke over 163, and the number of the g of chargé is under a blot with the letter over it blotted too. Image 39 not looked at. The key replay (replay.py, replay.tsv) decodes every number of the principal copy with key/key_positions.json: each letter of the reading that the key does not give is marked. A model's reading: no person has checked it.

texts.label: Despatch D and its Suite, September-October 1776 (in print)
texts.summary: Hortalez; Deane's and Arthur Lee's letters on Prussia and on France; the advice to aim at correspondence with "le ministre même"; Madam V. Loder as forwarding address. Printed in Sparks, Wharton and (images 52-53) Force.
texts.note: Read share over the cipher words only (the words between the cipher marks of the reading file; research/reading_audit measure, 24 Nov 2026): a word with a letter corrected or supplied by sense is a hole. 22 cipher words, 1 hole: Prussi[a] (the number of the second s is under a blot, with the decipherer's s over it; the next reads 25 = r where a is wanted). "King" is written cing: the key text has no k. By numbers: 114 of 116 give the reading's letter as transcribed (one of them c for k); one is a blot.

reading_review.by: integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person

The key replay (replay.py, replay.tsv) decodes every number of the principal copy with key/key_positions.json: each letter of the reading that the key does not give is marked. texts.summary: Copies of letters from the French ministers at The Hague, the abbé Desnoyers and the duc de La Vauguyon; printed in Sparks 9:310-311.
texts.note: Read share over the cipher words only (the words between the cipher marks of the reading file; research/reading_audit measure, 24 Nov 2026): a word with a letter corrected or supplied by sense is a hole. 19 cipher words, 1 hole: l'ab[b]é (the number is under an ink blot). 18 of 19 is 0.947, under 0.95: read by the short-text floor (fewer than 40 cipher words, at most 2 holes; README Conventions, 19 Nov 2026), recorded with floor_used, cipher_words and holes. reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading; it replaces the preliminary B recorded by the author's agents on 14 Nov 2026.
